title: Ayesa's absorption of Ibermatica increased independent scale, inverting the usual M&A effect in this corpus
content:
The flag on Ayesa records an acquisition that runs the other way. Where the other M&A notes in this corpus track independents being absorbed by listed groups, Ayesa's acquisition of Ibermatica is called out as one of the few that increased independent scale. The row records 13,200 staff and, unusually for this part of the dataset, an actual v3 score at medium confidence rather than a mechanical carry-over.

That makes the row a useful counter-example when reading the corpus as a whole. Consolidation is not uniformly hostile to the pilot's thesis: it can also produce a larger firm that still controls its own platform decisions, which is the property the screening cares about. Whether that holds for Ayesa is not established here — the flag asserts the direction of the change, not the firm's posture.

The tension on the row is that it still sits in the do-not-pitch tier. The flag does not say which input produced that placement, and with 13,200 staff recorded, scale is the obvious candidate; but the record does not state it, so the exclusion reason should be treated as unexplained rather than inferred.
